primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic kidney disease (stage 5 chronic kidney disease)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.medication: Humulin (insulin isophane 70 U/mL / regular insulin 30 U/mL)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review at each clinic visit
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for type 2 diabetes in advanced CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends tight glucose control in diabetic kidney disease; insulin is the preferred agent when eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control (first‑line antihypertensive in CKD)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 lists thiazide‑type diuretics as part of BP control strategy in CKD

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control (second‑line antihypertensive in CKD)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends CCBs as part of combination therapy for hypertension in CKD
Not a CKD‑specific recommendation; retained for current indication

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily (titrate by 2.5 mg every 2‑4 weeks to max 10 mg as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to reduce proteinuria and control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid panel at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong — review HbA1c and hypoglycaemia risk every 3‑6 months
medications.purpose: Additional glucose‑lowering; may reduce albuminuria and is safe down to eGFR ≈15 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: While NG203 does not list GLP‑1‑RA, NICE TA775 supports use in diabetes with CKD when additional control is needed; safe in eGFR <30

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering; risk of hyperkalaemia from ACE‑I combined with potassium shifts from thiazide
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and creatinine 1‑2 weeks after initiation and after each uptitration; monitor for symptomatic hypotension

interactions_checked.interaction: Synergistic antihypertensive effect; generally well tolerated
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure after starting ramipril; no dose adjustment required

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin 20 mg (lower end of dose range); advise patient to report muscle pain; avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increasing hypoglycaemia risk
interactions_checked.action: Reduce prandial insulin dose by 10‑20 % when dulaglutide is started; educate on hypoglycaemia signs

contraindications.reason: eGFR 14.4 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin (already prescribed) – preferred glucose‑lowering agent in advanced CKD

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5 – NSAIDs accelerate progression and increase fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain if needed; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Guideline contraindication due to increased hyperkalaemia and AKI risk

Baseline serum potassium and liver function tests not available – must be obtained before starting ramipril and atorvastatin.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, or GLP‑1‑RA not documented – verify before prescribing.

treatment_summary: The plan adds ramipril (ACE‑I) and atorvastatin to address proteinuria, hypertension, and cardiovascular risk per NICE NG203, and introduces dulaglutide to improve glycaemic control while respecting the eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m². Existing antihypertensives (hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine) are continued. Interactions are monitored, contraindicated drugs (metformin, chronic NSAIDs, ACE‑I + ARB) are avoided, and regular labs (K+, creatinine, LFTs, lipids, HbA1c) are scheduled to ensure safety and efficacy.
